resources.string: Expander expands shortcut triggers you configure into full text as you type. It reads and replaces text in the field you are typing in, across all apps. All processing happens on your device and nothing is sent over the internet.
When you enable the accessibility service, Android lets Expander read the text you type in editable fields in other apps and replace it.

Expander watches for a shortcut trigger you have configured, such as \"brb\", and replaces it with the full text you set. Reading and replacing text in the focused field is the only way to expand shortcuts across every app.

All processing happens on your device, in memory, for the field you are currently typing in. Expander does not store the contents of other apps. It has no internet permission, so nothing is ever sent off your device. There are no analytics and no tracking.
Expander is a typing productivity tool. It is not an accessibility aid for people with disabilities.
You can turn the accessibility service off at any time in Android Settings under Accessibility.
